newsitem.title: OMAN: Saudi discounts reports on Khobar blast arrests.
newsitem.headline: Saudi discounts reports on Khobar blast arrests.

text.p: Saudi Arabia on Sunday played down media reports it had arrested some 40 Saudis for a truck bombing of a U.S. military complex in June, saying Saudi security officials were the only credible source of news.

"We cannot accept media reports as fact," Saudi Interior Minister Prince Nayef told Reuters. "Nothing can be said (about the case) unless it is by the Saudi security sources. And that will be the truth."

Prince Nayef was referring to media reports in October that Saudi security officials had been secretly holding 40 nationals for at least three months for alleged involvement in the blast at the Khobar housing complex in Dhahran, eastern Saudi Arabia.
Nineteen U.S. Air Force service members were killed in the bombing.
The reports also said Saudi authorities were convinced Iran backed a broad conspiracy behind the attack. Iran denied any role.
"We will say whatever concerns the (attack) when the investigations are completed," Prince Nayef said.

Five Americans and two Indians died in a blast that rocked a U.S.-run military training centre in the Saudi capital Riyadh on November 13, 1995. Four Saudis who confessed to the attack were executed in May.
